source.subject: Biology
source.unit: Unit 1 — Diversity in the Living World
source.source_scope: Only the content printed on PDF page 5 (printed page 14): end of the heterotrophic bacteria discussion, bacterial reproduction, Mycoplasma, Section 2.2 Kingdom Protista (introduction), Section 2.2.1 Chrysophytes, and Figure 2.3.

questions.question: Pathogenic bacteria are described on the page as causing damage to which of the following?
questions.explanation: The page says some bacteria are pathogens causing damage to human beings, crops, farm animals and pets.
questions.source_text: Some are pathogens causing damage to human beings, crops, farm animals and pets.

questions.question: Which diseases are named on the page as caused by bacteria?
questions.explanation: The page names cholera, typhoid, tetanus and citrus canker as well-known bacterial diseases.
questions.source_text: Cholera, typhoid, tetanus, citrus canker are well known diseases caused by different bacteria.

questions.question: Bacteria reproduce mainly by:
questions.explanation: The page says bacteria reproduce mainly by fission.

questions.question: Under unfavourable conditions, bacteria sometimes produce:
questions.explanation: The page says that under unfavourable conditions bacteria sometimes produce spores.
questions.source_text: Sometimes, under unfavourable conditions, they produce spores.

questions.question: The sort of sexual reproduction seen in bacteria involves:
options: A primitive type of DNA transfer from one bacterium to another
Fusion of two gametes to form a zygote
Fusion of two vegetative cells followed by karyogamy
questions.explanation: The page describes bacterial sexual reproduction as adopting a primitive type of DNA transfer from one bacterium to the other.
questions.source_text: adopting a primitive type of DNA transfer from one bacterium to the other.

questions.question: Which organisms completely lack a cell wall and are the smallest living cells known?
questions.explanation: The page says Mycoplasma completely lack a cell wall and are the smallest living cells known.
questions.source_text: The Mycoplasma are organisms that completely lack a cell wall. They are the smallest living cells known

questions.question: Which statements about Mycoplasma are correct?
options: Many are pathogenic in animals and plants
They are the smallest living cells known
They completely lack a cell wall
They have a rigid cell wall
questions.explanation: The page states the four correct features. A rigid cell wall is a feature of eubacteria, and Mycoplasma lack a cell wall.
questions.source_text: and can survive without oxygen. Many mycoplasma are pathogenic in animals and plants.

questions.question: Kingdom Protista includes:
options: All organisms with chitin in their walls
questions.explanation: The page says all single-celled eukaryotes are placed under Protista.
questions.source_text: All single-celled eukaryotes are placed under Protista

questions.question: The page says what may be 'a photosynthetic protistan' to one biologist may be to another:
questions.explanation: This shows the boundaries of Protista are not well defined.
questions.source_text: What may be ‘a photosynthetic protistan’ to one biologist may be ‘a plant’ to another.

questions.question: Which groups are included under Protista in this book?
questions.explanation: The page lists Chrysophytes, Dinoflagellates, Euglenoids, Slime moulds and Protozoans.
questions.source_text: we include Chrysophytes, Dinoflagellates, Euglenoids, Slime moulds and Protozoans under Protista.

questions.question: Members of Kingdom Protista are primarily:
questions.explanation: The page says members of Protista are primarily aquatic.
questions.source_text: Members of Protista are primarily aquatic.

questions.question: Being eukaryotes, the protistan cell body contains:
options: A well defined nucleus and other membrane-bound organelles
Only a cell wall of chitin
questions.explanation: The page says the protistan cell body has a well defined nucleus and other membrane-bound organelles.
questions.source_text: the protistan cell body contains a well defined nucleus and other membrane-bound organelles.

questions.question: Protists reproduce asexually and sexually by a process involving:
questions.explanation: The page says the sexual process in protists involves cell fusion and zygote formation.
questions.source_text: Protists reproduce asexually and sexually by a process involving cell fusion and zygote formation.

questions.question: Chrysophytes include:
questions.explanation: The page says this group includes diatoms and golden algae (desmids).
questions.source_text: This group includes diatoms and golden algae (desmids).

questions.question: The cell walls of diatoms are:
options: Two thin overlapping shells embedded with silica
questions.explanation: The page says diatom walls form two thin overlapping shells that fit together like a soap box and are embedded with silica.
questions.source_text: the cell walls form two thin overlapping shells, which fit together as in a soap box. The walls are embedded with silica

questions.question: 'Diatomaceous earth' is formed by:
options: Accumulation of diatom cell wall deposits over billions of years
questions.explanation: The page says diatoms left behind large amounts of cell wall deposits and their accumulation over billions of years is called diatomaceous earth.
questions.source_text: this accumulation over billions of years is referred to as ‘diatomaceous earth’.

questions.question: Diatomaceous earth is used for:
questions.explanation: The page says being gritty, this soil is used in polishing and filtration of oils and syrups.
questions.source_text: this soil is used in polishing, filtration of oils and syrups.

questions.question: Which organisms are the chief 'producers' in the oceans?
questions.explanation: The page says diatoms are the chief producers in the oceans.
questions.source_text: Diatoms are the chief ‘producers’ in the oceans.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Diatom cell walls are indestructible.
Reason (R): The cell walls of diatoms are embedded with silica.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.explanation: The page says the walls are embedded with silica and thus are indestructible.
questions.source_text: The walls are embedded with silica and thus the walls are indestructible.
